patch.value: Renew pinned pnpm Windows shell-launcher compatibility after dependency cooldown

PR 1375 review identifies the locked pnpm 11.10.0 shell launcher using POSIX NODE_PATH when selecting Windows node.exe. The repository .txt templates only compare actual installed output and do not generate launchers. Upstream pnpm 11.28.1 also fixes Windows CMD percent-path handling and Cygwin target paths: https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v11.28.1. npm reports publication 2026-09-28T07:33:45.016Z, so that version first satisfies the unchanged seven-day cooldown on 2026-10-05T07:33:45.016Z; 11.28.2 is published later the same day. Evaluate a then-eligible supported version with real mixed-runtime fixtures instead of changing comparison templates independently of the installed generator. The verification edge to pm-q1ke preserves the completed pinned-installer bootstrap invariants when this future renewal is undertaken.

Retain the seven-day dependency cooldown; align packageManager and every CI/release/example pnpm pin; inspect actual published generator types/source and renew complete templates from real installation; run Windows Git Bash/Cygwin node.exe and POSIX Node dependency-resolution controls; verify quoted/percent paths, exact inventory, complete source coverage and all existing mandatory gates
Renew pinned generator output and prove Windows shell runtime path compatibility
Windows Node receives native path syntax while POSIX Node retains POSIX paths
Native review found a distinct upstream mixed-runtime compatibility concern while validating CodSpeed bundle admission
A supported cooldown-eligible pnpm generator preserves module and target paths across Windows and POSIX runtimes without weakening installed-artifact admission

Upstream release and registry dates are verified. Locked-template admission is strengthened in the current delivery; mixed-runtime generator renewal is queued and unclaimed, with no adoption or full interoperability claim.
